prompt: Comment on one of the following statements. University education is essential for young people. One cannot make real friends online. What is your opinion? Do you agree with this statement? Write 200 – 250 words . Use the following plan: – make an introduction (state the problem paraphrasing the given statement) – express your personal opinion and give 2 – 3 reasons for your opinion – express an opposing opinion and give 1 – 2 reasons for this opposing opinion – explain why you do not agree with the opposing opinion – make a conclusion restating your position
ideas: Intro: paraphrase — is a degree truly necessary for the young?
Agree: university gives deep knowledge, qualifications, useful connections
Agree: higher earnings and better career prospects long-term
Opposing: trades and self-taught skills can succeed without degrees
Rebut: most stable professions still legally require formal education
Conclude: degree opens more doors, so I support the statement
model:
Nowadays people often argue about whether a university degree is truly necessary for the young. Some regard it as absolutely essential, while others consider it merely optional.

In my opinion, higher education is indeed essential for young people. Firstly, university provides deep knowledge and recognised qualifications that many professions clearly demand. Secondly, it helps students build useful professional connections that can support them for years. Moreover, graduates usually enjoy higher earnings and better long-term career prospects than those who have no degree at all.

However, some people believe that university is not necessary. They point out that skilled tradespeople and self-taught specialists, especially in modern information technology, can succeed and earn well without any formal diploma.

Nevertheless, I cannot fully accept this position. Although a few talented individuals do prosper without degrees, most stable and respected professions, such as medicine or law, still legally require formal education. Therefore, relying on such rare exceptions would be extremely risky for an average young person planning a career.

To sum up, while occasional success without a diploma is certainly possible, university education remains essential for the majority. It opens more doors, offers greater security and prepares young people far better for an increasingly competitive future.

prompt: Comment on the following statement. Clothes people are wearing can influence their behaviour. What is your opinion? Do you agree with this statement? Write 200 – 250 words . ideas: Intro: do clothes really shape how we act?
Agree: formal wear boosts confidence and focus at interviews
Agree: uniforms create discipline; sportswear motivates activity
Opposing: character, not fabric, decides real behaviour
Rebut: psychology shows 'enclothed cognition' affects mindset measurably
Conclude: clothing influences mood and conduct, so I agree
model:
People often wonder whether the clothes we wear can actually shape the way we behave. This is a controversial issue on which opinions clearly differ.

I firmly believe that clothing does influence our behaviour. Firstly, formal wear tends to boost confidence and concentration, which is exactly why people feel more serious during interviews and examinations. Secondly, uniforms create a sense of discipline and belonging, while comfortable sportswear naturally encourages us to move and stay active. Moreover, dressing neatly often improves our mood for the entire day.

However, some people argue that clothes have no real effect on conduct. According to them, it is a person's character, and not the fabric they happen to wear, that truly decides how they act.

Nevertheless, I cannot agree with this claim. Psychologists have described an effect known as "enclothed cognition", showing that what we wear can measurably change our mindset and even our performance. Therefore, clothing clearly does far more than simply cover the body.

In conclusion, I remain convinced that our clothes influence both our mood and our conduct. The way we dress sends powerful signals to ourselves as well as to the people around us, and it quietly shapes the way we behave every day.
